en.sup: Supplied in English. The Greek verb has no object; the coin is meant.

01.r: The questioners, who produce the coin.
01.n: The Greek article standing alone with δέ, used as a pronoun: Abbott-Smith's first use of the article, 'he (she, it)'.

02.r: Moves from Jesus's request to their response.

03.r: They bring the coin Jesus asked to see.
03.n: Abbott-Smith's first sense is 'to bear, carry'. The YLT alone leaves the verb without an object, as the Greek does.

05.r: Jesus puts his question to them.
05.n: The present tense in a past narrative, kept here as in the KJV, DRC, ASV and YLT. The BSB's 'asked' names the kind of speech.

07.r: Asks to whom the image and inscription belong.
07.n: A genitive of the interrogative, literally 'of whom'. It covers both nouns: whose image, and whose inscription.

08.r: With 'this', points to the image on the coin in front of them.

09.r: The likeness stamped on the coin.
09.n: Abbott-Smith gives 'an image, likeness', notes that the Septuagint uses it chiefly for Hebrew צֶלֶם, and also records the word used of man as the 'image of God'. Whether Mark means a reader to make that connection here is not stated.

10.r: The image on the coin they have just handed over.

11.r: Joins the second thing Jesus asks about.

12.r: The particular inscription on this coin.

13.r: The words stamped on the coin around the image.
13.n: Abbott-Smith gives 'an inscription' and derives it from ἐπιγράφω, to write on. The KJV's 'superscription' is a Latin-based word with the same build, 'writing upon'.

18.r: Their one-word answer: the image and inscription are Caesar's.
